زَانٌ Indigestion; syn. بَشَمٌ; for النَّشَمُ in the copies of the K is a mistranscription for البَشَمُ; (TA;) expl. by Ed-Dubeyreeyeh as syn. with تُخْمَةٌ; as in the phrase, لَيْسَ يَشْكُو الزَّانَ [He does not complain of indigestion]: (Fr, TA:) and so
↓ زَانَةٌ : (K and TA in art. زين:) or this signifies a single fit of indigestion. (TA in that art.) ＝
-A2- [In the present day, applied to The beech-tree; and its wood: as a coll. gen. n.: n. un. with ة: see also زَانَةٌ below.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
